title: Constructible exceptional Frobenius mate, lifted adjunction and comparisons
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. Use the constructible adjunction $F=Rf_!\dashv G=Rf^!$ on $D^b_c$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, for every such $f$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Put $S=P_X$, $T=P_Y$, and assume their exact equivalences with inverse Frobenius transport and the canonical compact-support exchange isomorphism $a:TF\simeq FS$ of [def-exchange-projection], including its rational/common-stage construction. Give $F$ its Weil structure $F(\theta_K)a_K$. Then the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]
$$ b:SG\xrightarrow{\eta SG}GFSG\xrightarrow{Ga^{-1}G}GTFG\xrightarrow{GT\varepsilon}GT $$
is an isomorphism, and $(L,\theta_L)\mapsto(GL,G(\theta_L)b_L)$, with arrow $G(u)$, defines a Weil lift of this same constructible $G$. Its unit and counit are Weil morphisms and satisfy the adjunction triangle identities after forgetting. More explicitly the mate obeys
$$ (Ga)(bF)(S\eta)=\eta S,\qquad (\varepsilon T)(Fb)(aG)=T\varepsilon, $$
and the induced structures obey
$$ \theta_{GFK}S(\eta_K)=\eta_K\theta_K,\qquad \varepsilon_L\theta_{FGL}=\theta_LT(\varepsilon_L). $$

On their stated constructible domains, use the standard Frobenius lifts of pullback, direct images, tensor and internal Hom, and the canonical comparisons of [def-exchange-projection]. Composition comparisons, exchange transformations, tensor evaluation, ordinary adjunction maps and the projection transformation are Weil morphisms. Composition, whiskering by these lifted functors and inversion of isomorphisms preserve the Weil-morphism equations. The unit–map–counit mate of any such comparison under the lifted exceptional adjunction is again equivariant; the mate-pasting identities identify these maps with the specified exceptional composition/exchange maps. Thus every such comparison already known to be invertible is an isomorphism of Weil pairs on exactly its proved domain. In the Frobenius square $a=\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is invertible also when the base is non-separated, after rationalization and in the common-stage category. No ambient exceptional right adjoint or separatedness of $X_0,Y_0$ is assumed. Equivariance alone makes no new comparison invertible.

source.place: Proof sentence 1: exceptional adjunction, its unit/counit, comparison maps and mate pasting; returned proof Steps 3–4 and 6.

proof.text: Work in the specified rational or common-stage categories themselves. The assumed adjunction is the constructible $F\dashv G$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; its unit and counit therefore have exactly these categories as domain. The given $S,T$ are equivalences. Independently, [lem-pod-weil-frobenius-compact-support-exchange] states that the specified $a=\operatorname{Ex}_!:TF\to FS$ is a natural isomorphism on the supplied domains, including the rational/common-stage categories and non-separated $X_0,Y_0$. Thus the last assertion about this particular exchange is already available. Keep its coefficient and finite-Tor domain restrictions throughout. No ambient exceptional adjoint is used.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] with both adjunctions equal to $F\dashv G$, the non-adjoint sides $S,T$, and square $\alpha=a^{-1}:FS\to TF$. Its displayed component formula is precisely $b_L=GT(\varepsilon_L)\,G(a^{-1}_{GL})\,\eta_{SGL}$. In [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] take $L=L'=F$, $R=R'=G$, $G_{\rm there}=S$, $G'_{\rm there}=T$, and $\theta=a^{-1}$. The first side is an equivalence and the second is fully faithful because $T$ is an equivalence. That theorem makes this same $b:SG\to GT$ a natural isomorphism. This uses the equivalence hypotheses, not a general assertion that square mates preserve isomorphisms.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: The unit identity of [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility], with $\alpha=a^{-1}$, gives $b_{FK}S(\eta_K)=G(a_K^{-1})\eta_{SK}$. Postcompose with $G(a_K)$ to obtain $G(a_K)b_{FK}S(\eta_K)=\eta_{SK}$. The transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives $\varepsilon_{TL}F(b_L)=T(\varepsilon_L)a^{-1}_{GL}$. Precompose with $a_{GL}$ to obtain $\varepsilon_{TL}F(b_L)a_{GL}=T(\varepsilon_L)$. These are the two asserted mate equations, with every component typed in the constructible categories.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text:
Set $\theta_{GL}=G(\theta_L)b_L$, an isomorphism since both factors are isomorphisms. For a Weil arrow $u:L\to L'$, naturality of $b$ and the equation $u\theta_L=\theta_{L'}T(u)$ give
$$G(u)G(\theta_L)b_L=G(\theta_{L'})G(Tu)b_L=G(\theta_{L'})b_{L'}S(G(u)).$$
Thus $G(u)$ is a Weil arrow. Its identity and composition laws are the ones of the same underlying $G$. The analogous computation with naturality of $a$ gives the stated lift $\theta_{FK}=F(\theta_K)a_K$. These are actual functors on the categories of pairs in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text:
For $K$ on $X$, the structure of $GFK$ is $GF(\theta_K)G(a_K)b_{FK}$. By Step 3 and naturality of $\eta$,
$$\theta_{GFK}S(\eta_K)=GF(\theta_K)\eta_{SK}=\eta_K\theta_K.$$
For $L$ on $Y$, the structure of $FGL$ is $FG(\theta_L)F(b_L)a_{GL}$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ and Step 3 give
$$\varepsilon_L\theta_{FGL}=\theta_L\varepsilon_{TL}F(b_L)a_{GL}=\theta_LT(\varepsilon_L).$$
Consequently the original unit and counit are Weil morphisms, with no replacement of their underlying maps.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: The two triangle equations are the original equations of the assumed $F\dashv G$ and still hold after forgetting. They hold as equations of Weil morphisms as well, since the forgetful functor of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is faithful. Explicitly a Weil map $h:FK\to L$ has transpose $G(h)\eta_K$, which is Weil by Steps 4–5; a Weil map $v:K\to GL$ has inverse transpose $\varepsilon_LF(v)$, also Weil. These restrictions of the original Hom bijections are inverse by the triangles. This supplies the lifted adjunction, including naturality, rather than just equivariant functors.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text:
We will use the following elementary equation test. If $H,J$ have Frobenius comparisons $c_H:PH\to HQ$, $c_J:PJ\to JQ$, a natural transformation $d:H\to J$ induces a map of pairs whenever
$$d_{QK}c_{H,K}=c_{J,K}P(d_K).$$
Indeed multiply this equality on the left by $J(\theta_K)$ and use naturality $d_KH(\theta_K)=J(\theta_K)d_{QK}$. For Weil arrows $u,v$, $(vu)\theta=v\theta'P(u)=\theta''P(vu)$. If $u$ is invertible, multiplying $u\theta=\theta'P(u)$ by the inverses gives $u^{-1}\theta'=\theta P(u^{-1})$. Applying a lifted functor sends the equation for $u$ to the equation for its image, by naturality of that functor's comparison. Thus composition, both whiskerings by lifted functors, and inverses preserve equivariance; the forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: For ordinary adjunctions put $L=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$. Use only the constructible domains of the ordinary adjunction in [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). The comparison $P_XL\simeq LP_Y$ is pullback composition in the Frobenius square. By the explicit definition of $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ in [def-exchange-projection], the mate of its inverse is exactly the standard comparison $P_YR\to RP_X$: its transpose is the pullback square followed by the ordinary counit. Consequently the calculations in Steps 3–6, replacing $(F,G,S,T)$ by $(L,R,P_Y,P_X)$, prove equivariance of both ordinary adjunction maps for the specified standard lifts. No exceptional-admissibility clause of [fix-prop-adjunctions] is invoked.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: For pullbacks along composable morphisms, expand the Frobenius comparison using the pullback-composition maps. The two maps from $P_XL(gf)^*$ to $Lf^*Lg^*P_Z$ are the two associative expansions of that composition; the associativity identity of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] identifies them before rationalization. Their rational images and their common-stage classes are therefore equal, by the definitions in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. This is the equation test of Step 7 for the pullback composition comparison. For tensor the composition compatibility and naturality of $\mu$ in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] give the same equation test for tensor-pullback comparisons; its associativity, symmetry and unit clauses give it for the tensor structure comparisons. All inputs and outputs are restricted to the already specified constructible domains.

proof.text: Frobenius is semilinear over $k$, so apply the $k$-linear diagram theorems after the following relabeling. Replace the structural map $a_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at a source corner of $g_W$ by $a_Wg_W$. Then $g_W$ to the original corner is $k$-linear, and a morphism $r$ between two such relabeled corners is $k$-linear because $rg_W=g_Vr$. These are still finite-type $k$-schemes: $g_W$ identifies each relabeled scheme with its original one. The sites, constant coefficient categories and underlying operation maps are unchanged, since the definitions depend on the underlying scheme morphisms. Thus all Frobenius faces of a composition diagram or exchange cube are diagrams to which [fix-lem-exchanges] applies. Its hypotheses require separated finite-type arrows and finite-type schemes, not separated structure maps $a_W$. Base-changed compactifications and the isomorphism faces retain the required arrow hypotheses.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: Apply [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2),(4) to the relabeled diagrams of Step 10, first with $P=R(-)_*$ and then with $P=R(-)_!$. Vertical pasting says that exchange for a composite is the composite of the two exchanges with the direct-image composition comparison inserted. This is exactly Step 7's equation for that comparison. For an exchange square, paste a Frobenius square with it in either order; both composites are exchange for the same outside square by horizontal and vertical pasting. Inserting the pullback and direct-image comparisons just proved equivariant yields Step 7's equation for the exchange transformation itself. Clause (4) intertwines all these maps with compactification refinement comparisons, so this proves the assertion for the specified compact-support operation, independent of its chosen representative. Naturality in the input then inserts its Weil map as in Step 7. The coefficient, witnessed-origin and finite-Tor restrictions in [fix-lem-exchanges] remain in force.

proof.text:
Write $H(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$ and $P=P_W$. For the canonical Hom transport $h:PH(M,N)\to H(PM,PN)$, the definition as transpose under the tensor/Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations](i) is the identity
$$\operatorname{ev}_{PM,PN}(1\otimes h)\mu_{M,H(M,N)}=P(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}).$$
Here evaluation has domain $M\otimes H(M,N)$; this fixes the convention for $h$ in the standard lift. Naturality of evaluation in the isomorphisms $\theta_M:PM\to M$, $\theta_N:PN\to N$ gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}(\theta_M\otimes H(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N))=\theta_N\operatorname{ev}_{PM,PN}.$$
Compose these equalities. The tensor structure on $M\otimes H(M,N)$ is $(\theta_M\otimes H(\theta_M^{-1},\theta_N)h)\mu$, so the result is exactly $\operatorname{ev}\,\theta_{M\otimes H}=\theta_NP(\operatorname{ev})$. This proves evaluation equivariant on its stated domain, without inferring site-perfectness of arbitrary constructible objects.

proof.text: For the ordinary projection transformation $\pi$ in [def-exchange-projection], its transpose $a_{u,M,N}$ is tensor-pullback followed by $\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1$. Both are equivariant by Steps 8–9, and $\pi=Ru_*(a)\eta$ is equivariant by Step 7. For the open projection comparison $\gamma$, compare its pullback under the compactification's Frobenius base-change map with the corresponding $\gamma'$ for $j'$. Apply $j'^*$ to this square, inserting the open base-change maps $\beta$ and the tensor/pullback comparisons. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], $j'^*\beta$ and the restrictions of $\gamma,\gamma'$ are identities after the open-unit identifications; the remaining square is the tensor/pullback composition equation from Step 9. Both original source and target are in the essential image of $j'_!$: use $\beta$ and $\gamma'$ to identify the source as well. Full faithfulness of $j'_!$ and its invertible unit, asserted in that same node, therefore reflect the restricted equality. This proves the required open comparison equation. Its strict-coefficient-system version in that node and the supplied higher-stage comparisons in [def-exchange-projection] retain this equation in the specified coefficient constructions. Now $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}=Rp_*(\gamma)\pi_p$ is equivariant by composition and Step 11's compactification independence, on exactly its supplied tensor and finite-Tor domains.

proof.text: A mate of any comparison now proved equivariant has, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], three factors: a whiskered unit, the comparison under the appropriate lifted functors, and a whiskered counit. Steps 5–8 and 7 make each factor a Weil morphism, hence their composite is one. To identify it with an exceptional composition or exchange map, use [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) for pasting on the non-adjoint sides, (2) for composition of adjunctions, and (3) for changing the adjunctions by the ordinary or compact-support comparison. These formulas identify the mate of the pasted square with the pasted mates for the very adjunctions fixed here. The bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] ensures equality with the specified unit–map–counit definition, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of functors. In particular the conjugate of a composition comparison is equivariant; when it is invertible its inverse is equivariant by Step 7.

source.place: Sentence 1: exceptional adjunction and equivariant algebraic comparisons; detailed mate calculation

proof.text: These calculations take place in the rational/common-stage categories, so they apply to all their morphisms, including Weil maps without an invariant integral lattice. When a comparison is represented integrally, apply rationalization to its defining composites, and then take their classes over one common finite field, exactly as specified in [def-exchange-projection] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Functors preserve the equality of these composites. Further coefficient extension conjugates source and target by the supplied comparison isomorphisms; the two adjacent intermediate comparisons cancel. Their identity and tower cocycles make the resulting equality independent of the representative. For every comparison whose invertibility is already known on this domain, Step 7 shows that its actual inverse is a Weil arrow, hence gives an isomorphism of Weil pairs. Nothing in this reasoning enlarges the domain or proves invertibility of another exchange or projection map.
